newsitem.title: THAILAND: Jackson fails to draw sellout Thai crowd.
newsitem.headline: Jackson fails to draw sellout Thai crowd.

text.p: Pop superstar Michael Jackson's concert on Tuesday in Thailand has not sold out, with only about 70 percent of the 50,000 tickets having been bought so far, concert organisers said.
Sales are a far cry from the sell-out in 1993 when thousands of disappointed fans tore down the iron gates of the National Stadium in Bangkok to catch a glimpse of the singer in concert.
His second show was delayed for two days when Jackson said he was dehydrated and could not perform as scheduled. But when he was declared fit again, the show went on to a packed house.
"So far about 70 percent of the tickets have been sold and we don't expect to get more fans," Natawadi Patanawong, a promotion manager for the concert, told Reuters.
She said the venue of the concert, in the Muangthong Thani housing estate on the far northeastern fringe of Bangkok, could have been a reason for the slower than expected sales.
"But this time his health is superb," said Natawadi, allaying any fear that the show might be postponed or cancelled.
